label: Mass used (of the mass limit)
why: Real designs keep about 20% mass margin because parts always grow heavier during building.
fix: Downgrade heavy parts: propulsion and the big battery are the heaviest.

label: Rocket capacity used
why: A rocket cannot lift more than its capacity to that orbit.
fix: Pick a rocket that reaches this orbit with more capacity.

label: Budget used
why: Keep a reserve for surprises; going over the budget cancels the mission.
fix: Cheaper parts, a rideshare rocket or a shorter mission.

label: Power margin (solar average vs use)
why: Below 0% the panels cannot keep up and the payload is switched off part of each day.
fix: Deployable solar array, or drop power-hungry parts (ion thruster, heaters, FPGA).

label: Battery discharge per eclipse
why: Only about 60% of a battery can be used safely each orbit; deeper discharges trigger safe mode and wear it out.
fix: The bigger battery, or less power used during eclipse.

label: Data made vs radio capacity
why: Above 100% the radio cannot send everything and images are lost.
fix: A faster radio (X-band) or a less data-hungry payload.

label: Days of data the memory can hold
why: If a ground pass is missed the data must wait onboard.
fix: More storage (FPGA computer) or less data.

label: Useful data vs requirement
why: Below 100% the data requirement is failed.
fix: Precision pointing (sharper images), a better payload or a faster radio.

label: Revisit vs requirement
why: Above 100% the area is seen less often than required.

label: Orbit life vs planned lifetime
why: The spacecraft must stay in orbit for the whole planned mission.
fix: Higher orbit, propulsion or a shorter plan.

label: Planned lifetime vs requirement
why: The mission must be planned for at least the required years.
fix: Increase the planned lifetime at the console.
